items.label: list_item
items.text: Know that a hydrocarbon is a compound made up of hydrogen and carbon only

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand how to represent organic molecules using empirical formulae, molecular formulae, general formulae, structural formulae and displayed formulae

items.label: list_item
items.text: Know what is meant by the terms homologous series, functional group and isomerism

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand how to name compounds (containing up to six carbon atoms) using the rules of International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) nomenclature

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand how to write the possible structural and displayed formulae of an organic molecule given its molecular formula

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand how to classify reactions of organic compounds as substitution, addition and combustion

items.label: text
items.text: In the next few chapters we will be looking at organic compounds. The term 'organic' was originally used because it was believed that organic compounds could only come from living things. Now it is used for any carbon compound except for the very simplest (carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, the carbonates and the hydrogencarbonates).

items.label: text
items.text: Organic compounds can exist as chains, branched chains or rings of carbon atoms with hydrogens attached.

items.label: text
items.text: When you start doing organic chemistry, you are suddenly faced with a whole lot of new compounds with strange names and unfamiliar ways of drawing them. It can be quite scary!
